Factor by Box Method

Another way to factor a polynomial with four terms. Have your notebook open to pages 62–63.

4x2 − 36x + 7x − 63  ⟶  (4x + 7)(x − 9)

Page 63

Factor by Box Method: the steps

  • 1.Factor out any GCF first
  • 2.Put the 4 terms in a 2×2 box like below
  • 3.Find the GCF of each row and column. Write these outside.
  • 4.Write the factors as binomials.

Page 63 · Where everything goes

×GCF of column 1GCF of column 2
GCF of row 1highest degree term heremiddle term
GCF of row 2middle termlowest degree term here
Tip

The two middle terms can go in either spot. Only the corners have to be exact.

Example 2, again Extra · not in your notes

What if we swap the middle terms?

×2x²−1
x2x³−x
36x²−3
Same answer

(2x² − 1)(x + 3). The middle terms can go either way.

Review

Four things to watch for

1

GCF first. If all four terms share a GCF, factor it out first and keep it in your answer.

2

Corners. Highest degree term top left. Lowest degree term bottom right.

3

Signs. Pick the sign that makes the multiplication work, like −9 instead of 9.

4

Check. Side × top should equal every box inside.

Wrap-up

You've got it

  1. Factor out any GCF first.
  2. Put the four terms in the box. Highest and lowest degree go in the corners.
  3. Find the GCF of each row and column. Write them outside.
  4. Read the top and the side as two binomials. done

Check: side × top should equal every box inside.

Optional

Practice on your own

Six problems. For each one:

  1. Draw the box in your notebook and work it out.
  2. Stuck? Hint 1 shows the terms in the box. Hint 2 shows the outside.
  3. Pick your answer to check it. Wrong answers tell you what to fix.
